decisions.reason: The footer background color change does not alter the required legal-document links or their accessibility.
The requirement to reuse the same footer across webpages remains unchanged; the footer's specific background treatment is already owned by the source Requirement.
The provisioning wizard's footer remains optional, and the source decision does not change its required background, header logo, or footer-inclusion rule.
The source concerns the website footer, not the independently styled SaaS console shell footer.
The sign-in page continues to use a landing-page-based background and header logo; the website footer color change does not alter those requirements.
The client rejects purple only as too dominant for the footer; the decision does not change the landing-page hero's purple background.
The footer background treatment does not affect the How It Works section's position, presentation, or steps.
Changing the footer color does not modify the reusable responsive breakpoint guidance.
The source selects a footer-specific color but does not necessarily revise the requested design-system deliverables or resolve their outstanding scope ambiguity.
The footer color decision does not change the plain HTML, Tailwind CSS, or no-Astro implementation stack.
The footer background color does not alter the landing page's responsive layout behavior.
The footer background treatment does not change which follow-on copy is included on the landing page.
